cover.explanation: This PR is a docs fix: the Limitations list in the base-branch docs/embeddable/backends.md contradicts the base-branch documentation, and the diff only aligns it with that documentation. The 'flm ... not available for packaging-time bundling on Linux' claim is stale because docs/guide/faq.md already states 'Today, NPU-only inference on Linux is available via FastFlowLM', and the blanket llamacpp:rocm claim is stale because docs/guide/configuration/llamacpp.md documents the default stable channel as shipping 'Common builds for supported architectures', with only the nightly channel using architecture-specific builds. The added blank line restores rendering of the list that was failing to render on the base branch, so every change is a fix and no working-group charter or RFC is required.

explanation.body: The title, body, and template claims describe what the diff does.
explanation.diff: The diff touches only docs/embeddable/backends.md: it removes the outdated claim that flm cannot be packaging-time bundled on Linux, rewrites the llamacpp:rocm entry so the limitation applies only when rocm_channel is nightly (stable is unaffected), and inserts a blank line before the list to fix rendering on zensical. The body's claims of two stale-limitation fixes plus one formatting fix match the diff exactly.
explanation.quality: Opened docs/embeddable/backends.md at the head SHA and verified both corrections against the install code at the same SHA: fastflowlm_server.cpp ships a fastflowlm_<ver>_linux.tar.gz asset (dropped flm-on-Linux claim is stale), and llamacpp_server.cpp builds rocm-stable asset names without a GPU family but derives rocm-nightly names from SystemInfo::get_rocm_arch() at install time, matching the new rocm_channel wording; a docs-tree search found no sibling page repeating the dropped claims. Testing is n/a per testing.md's docs-only row — no testable surface, and the no-link-change diff has nothing for markdown-link-check to flag.
